crop: Chili pepper / hot pepper / piment (Capsicum frutescens and Capsicum chinense: Safi, Big Sun, Antillais, Salmon, Jaune du Burkina, Langue d'oiseau), open field, Cameroon
pilot_zone_context: Foumbot (Noun, West Cameroon) and the main Cameroon supply basins named in market reports (East and West regions); sold fresh by 50 or 100 kg bag in Yaounde markets (Mendong, Mfoundi, Mokolo).

detail.note: About 35 days in nursery; transplant about 1.5 months after sowing
6 to 7 weeks, seedlings 15 to 20 cm with 4 to 5 leaves
4 to 5 weeks, 4 to 5 true leaves (Caribbean guide)
3 to 4 months after transplanting; about 1.5 months after flowering
3 to 4 months after transplanting; about 10 weeks after flowering
Big Sun (C. chinense): first harvest 90 days after transplanting
Harvest window up to 4 months (S1); 3 to 4 months (S2)
Up to 6 months under irrigation, weekly picking

harvest_frequency.text: Weekly (S9). Pick mature fruit with the stalk, in dry weather (S1).

seasons.text: Sowing in February (main season) and August (counter season); best yields in the counter season, July to August (S1).

spacing.text: 80 cm x 80 cm (S1, S2). Both sheets state 13,750 plants/ha, which does not match the spacing: 80 x 80 cm gives 15,625 plants/ha (analyst arithmetic). Technisem advises 15,000 to 17,000 plants/ha for Big Sun (S7).

seed_rate.text: About 1.5 kg/ha in the Cameroon sheets (S1, S2, S10). Technisem: 400 to 600 g/ha for Big Sun, 230 to 280 seeds per gram (S7). 100 g holds about 20,000 seeds (S9).

nursery.text: Beds 20 cm high and 1 m wide, rows 20 cm apart, seed 2 cm deep (S1). About 200 m2 of nursery per ha (S1, S2, S10). Poultry manure 5 kg/m2 two weeks before sowing, then NPK 20-10-10 at 50 g per linear metre two weeks after emergence (S1). Shade, daily watering (S2).

basal.text: Holes 20 cm deep dug a week before transplanting; 1 kg poultry manure per hole (S1). 1 kg manure plus two teaspoons of potassium sulphate per hole (S2).

schedule.when: Two weeks after the basal manure
First fruit set, then after each harvest

pests_diseases.text: Downy mildew and alternaria leaf spot, favoured by heavy rain (S1). Nursery and field sprays of maneb and cypermethrin from two weeks after sowing: weekly in the rainy season, every two weeks in the dry season, and after each harvest; copper fungicide alternated with maneb (S1). The sheet adds a carbofuran nematicide (Furadan type) in the basal dressing; carbofuran is a highly hazardous pesticide.

national_average.note: FAOSTAT 'Chillies and peppers, green', Cameroon; mixes hot and sweet peppers (see pepper.json P14).

cameroon_sheets.note: Hybrid varieties, 12,000 kg/ha per year as stated; Langue d'oiseau under 3.5 t/ha
10 to 20 t/ha depending on variety, more for some improved varieties
10 to 15 t/ha under good conditions; national production over 120,000 t a year

irrigated_export_reference.note: St Vincent, 2 ft x 3 ft and 2 ft x 4 ft, 36,000 and 30,000 lb/acre converted; far above African references

labour.harvest: South African vegetable budget, chilli pages: 10 t/ha picked in 1,900 hours (see pepper.json P25), about 42 kg per 8 hour day. St Vincent: 264 person days to pick 16.3 t on one acre, about 62 kg per day (S9).

prices.unit_notes: Fresh chili is sold wholesale by 50 kg or 100 kg bag and at retail by heap (tas). Per kg values are analyst divisions.

observations.note: Same period 2021: 20,000 to 25,000 FCFA per 100 kg (200 to 250 FCFA/kg)
6,000 FCFA per bag in a glut, 50,000 FCFA in a shortage; supply from the East and West regions

prices.notes: No published farm gate price. Urban wholesale prices swing by a factor of about 8 between glut and shortage.

value_added.text: Over 70% of production is sold raw on local markets; sauces and powders can fetch 4 to 5 times the value of a raw kilogram (S3). Drying after 30 to 40 minutes of boiling is described in S1.

confidence_notes: MEDIUM for agronomy: a Cameroon sheet hosted by MINADER (S1) and a Cameroon technical sheet (S2) agree on spacing, nursery and cycle. LOW for yields: Cameroon sheets give 10 to 20 t/ha against a national average near 2 t/ha. LOW for prices: only urban wholesale prices in Yaounde, very volatile; no farm gate price. Seed prices are Senegal listings (same CFA parity).
